docs.title: Jellyfin Control
docs.text:
Browse your Jellyfin library and drive every Jellyfin app from Home Assistant: playback, queue, tracks, navigation, messages and search, through the Jellyfin REST API only.

It runs next to the official jellyfin integration (domain jellyfin_control) and ships its own asynchronous REST client.

docs.title: What it adds over the official integration
docs.text:
Feature Official jellyfin Jellyfin Control Play, pause, stop, seek yes yes Next / previous track no yes Volume set, mute yes yes Volume up / down no yes Shuffle and repeat modes no yes Enqueue (play now, next, last) yes (single item) yes; folders, series, albums, artists, genres and playlists are expanded into a queue Audio and subtitle track selection no select entities and actions Remote navigation blocking, raw names async, with aliases (up, home, info...) and every general command Messages, text input, open an item page on the TV no yes Play queue as data no get_queue action Library browsing movies, shows, music every library type, Continue watching, Next up, Recently added, Favorites, artists/albums/songs, Live TV Search yes yes, plus a search_library action that returns data Mark played / favorite no yes Instant mix no yes Scan libraries no button (administrators) Entities survive a client restart no (keyed on session id) yes (keyed on device id); a disconnected client reads off Credentials stored username and password an access token only; sign in by password or Quick Connect; the token is revoked when the entry is deleted Stream to other players (media source) yes (URL carries the token) yes, relayed by Home Assistant: the token never leaves it

Start with Install, then Configuration.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
All take a jellyfin_control media player as target.

Action Does jellyfin_control.play_items Play or queue item ids (enqueue: play, next, add, replace), with shuffle, start_index, start_position. jellyfin_control.play_media_shuffle Play an item or folder shuffled. jellyfin_control.play_instant_mix Play a mix built from a song, album, artist or genre. jellyfin_control.seek_relative Move by ± seconds. jellyfin_control.seek_chapter Go to the next or previous chapter, or to a chapter by index. jellyfin_control.get_chapters Returns the chapters of the playing item and the current one. jellyfin_control.send_message Show a message on the TV. jellyfin_control.send_text Type into the focused field (search box). jellyfin_control.send_command Any general command, with arguments. jellyfin_control.display_content Open an item's page in the app. jellyfin_control.set_audio_stream / set_subtitle_stream Switch tracks by index (-1 turns subtitles off). jellyfin_control.set_user_data Mark played / unplayed, favorite / not. jellyfin_control.get_queue Returns the play queue. jellyfin_control.browse_library Returns the children of a folder (root, special:resume, special:next_up, special:latest, special:favorites, latest:<library id> for the newest items of one library, any item id). jellyfin_control.search_library Returns matching items.

Remote commands accept these aliases: up, down, left, right, select (ok), back, home, menu, info (osd), stats, fullscreen, settings, search, context_menu, page_up, page_down, channel_up, channel_down, guide, volume_up, volume_down, mute, play_pause, play, pause, stop, next, previous, rewind, fast_forward. Any other name is sent as a Jellyfin general command.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
actions:
  - action: jellyfin_control.search_library
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.living_room
    data:
      query: "The Matrix"
      media_types: [movie]
      limit: 1
    response_variable: found
  - action: jellyfin_control.play_items
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.living_room
    data:
      item_ids: "{{ found['media_player.living_room'].items[0].id }}"

More in the documentation.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Action Fields play_items item_ids (required, comma separated), enqueue (play default, next, add, replace), shuffle (default false), start_index, start_position (seconds) play_media_shuffle media (required, media selector) play_instant_mix item_id (required) seek_relative seconds (required, negative goes back) seek_chapter chapter (required: next, previous or an index from get_chapters, 0 is the first) get_chapters none send_message message (required), title, timeout (seconds, default 5) send_text text (required) send_command command (required, Jellyfin general command name), arguments (object) display_content item_id (required) set_audio_stream, set_subtitle_stream index (required; -1 turns subtitles off) set_user_data item_id (required), played, favorite browse_library parent_id (root when empty), limit (default 100, at most 1000; the rest is counted in not_shown) search_library query (required), media_types, limit (default 50, 1-500) get_queue none

An action needing a command the client does not advertise (for example seek_relative without seek support, track selection without SetAudioStreamIndex) is refused before anything is sent. send_command and raw remote commands are the escape hatch and are never filtered.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
browse_library and search_library return items shaped like:

items:
  - id: 9f2c0d7e5b8a4c1f9e3d2b6a7c8d9e0f
    title: The Matrix (1999)
    name: The Matrix
    type: Movie
    media_class: movie
    can_play: true
    can_expand: false
    year: 1999
    duration: 8160
    played: false
    favorite: true

get_queue returns position, id, title, type and current for each queue entry.

get_chapters returns position (seconds), current (index of the chapter being played, empty without chapters) and chapters, each with index, name and start (seconds). Chapters are read from the item on each call: sessions do not carry them.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Module Role api.py JellyfinClient: async REST client on Home Assistant's aiohttp session. No Home Assistant import; raises its own errors. Encodes every path segment, follows no redirect. coordinator.py Polls /Sessions, keys them by device id, drops Home Assistant's own session and the server's. library.py The library tree as plain LibraryNode values, search, folder-to-queue expansion and the play queue. Shared by the media player, the media source and the actions. entity.py Base entities, device info, call_api() that turns client errors into translated Home Assistant errors. media_player.py One player per device: state, controls, play media, browse and search, artwork proxy, action handlers. remote.py, select.py, sensor.py, button.py The other platforms. media_source.py The library as a media source; resolves to relayed stream paths. views.py Home Assistant views relaying artwork and streams with the token in a header (signed paths, Range pass-through). services.py Registration and schemas of the entity actions. config_flow.py Server, password or Quick Connect, reauth, reconfigure, options. diagnostics.py Entry dump without token, user id or client addresses.

The config entry stores the URL, the SSL flag, Home Assistant's own Jellyfin device id, the access token, the user id and the server id; never a password.

docs.title: Assist and MCP
docs.text: Assist offers intents only. None of them changes a select entity or calls an integration action, so a voice assistant could read the subtitles of a film but not turn them off. The integration therefore registers its own LLM API, Jellyfin Control, with one tool per control.

docs.title: Enable it
docs.text:
• MCP clients (Claude, other agents): in Settings > Devices & services > Model Context Protocol Server > Configure, select Jellyfin Control next to Assist. The client sees the tools after it reconnects.
  • Conversation agents (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama...): select Jellyfin Control in the agent's Control Home Assistant options.

Jellyfin Control (voice) is the same API with only the controls people say out loud: every tool below except jellyfin_seek_chapter, jellyfin_instant_mix, jellyfin_show_message, jellyfin_navigate, jellyfin_send_text, jellyfin_display_item, jellyfin_set_user_data and jellyfin_scan_library. Each tool definition is sent to the model on every step, so a voice assistant answers faster with 12 tools than with 20.

Only media players exposed to Assist (Settings > Voice assistants > Expose) can be targeted, as with the Assist API. The tools run the integration's actions as the requesting user, with the same checks: a command the client does not advertise is refused with the reason.

docs.title: Players
docs.text: Tools take an optional player: its name, an alias, its area or its entity id. It can be left out when a single player is connected. The prompt given to the model lists the players with their aliases, area and state.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool Does jellyfin_get_players State, playing item, position, volume, audio and subtitle tracks, last played item, supported features. jellyfin_search Search the library (query, media_types, limit). jellyfin_browse Browse: libraries, special:resume, special:next_up, special:latest, latest:LIBRARY_ID, any folder. jellyfin_get_queue The play queue. jellyfin_play Play item ids (enqueue, shuffle, start_position). jellyfin_playback play, pause, play_pause, stop, next, previous. jellyfin_seek offset in seconds (forward, negative goes back) or position from the start. jellyfin_get_chapters Chapters of the playing item and the current one. jellyfin_seek_chapter next, previous or a chapter index. jellyfin_volume level (0-100), mute, step (up/down). jellyfin_shuffle_repeat shuffle, repeat (off, all, one). jellyfin_set_subtitles track: off, an index, or a language or title (french, français). jellyfin_set_audio_track track: an index, or a language or title. jellyfin_instant_mix Play similar music from an item. jellyfin_show_message Show a message on screen. jellyfin_navigate Remote keys (up, down, select, back, home...), with repeats. jellyfin_send_text Type into the focused field. jellyfin_display_item Open an item's page. jellyfin_set_user_data Mark played or unplayed, favorite or not. jellyfin_scan_library Scan the libraries (administrators).

Read-only tools (jellyfin_get_players, jellyfin_search, jellyfin_browse, jellyfin_get_queue, jellyfin_get_chapters) stay available when the MCP server is set to read-only.

Track names come from Jellyfin, in English: French language names (anglais, allemand, japonais...) are translated before matching. Jellyfin applies the default subtitle track again to each new item, so subtitles turned off come back on the next episode unless the Jellyfin user settings say otherwise.

docs.title: Comparison with the official integration
docs.text:
Feature Official jellyfin Jellyfin Control Play, pause, stop, seek yes yes Next / previous track no yes Volume set, mute yes yes Volume up / down no yes Shuffle and repeat modes no yes Enqueue (play now, next, last) yes (single item) yes; folders, series, albums, artists, genres and playlists are expanded into a queue Audio and subtitle track selection no select entities and actions Remote navigation blocking, raw names async, with aliases (up, home, info...) and every general command Messages, text input, open an item page on the TV no yes Play queue as data no get_queue action Library browsing movies, shows, music every library type, Continue watching, Next up, Recently added, Favorites, artists/albums/songs, Live TV Search yes yes, plus a search_library action that returns data Mark played / favorite no yes Instant mix no yes Scan libraries no button (administrators) Entities survive a client restart no (keyed on session id) yes (keyed on device id); a disconnected client reads off Credentials stored username and password an access token only; sign in by password or Quick Connect; the token is revoked when the entry is deleted Stream to other players (media source) yes (URL carries the token) yes, relayed by Home Assistant: the token never leaves it

Both integrations can be installed together. To migrate, add Jellyfin Control, point automations to the new entity ids, then delete the official entry.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Server: the address, for example http://192.168.1.10:8096. A /jellyfin base path behind a reverse proxy is found automatically. Turn Verify SSL certificate off only for a self-signed certificate.
  2. Sign in, either:
  3. Username and password: exchanged once for an access token, then discarded;
  4. Quick Connect: enter the displayed code in a Jellyfin app already signed in (Settings → Quick Connect), then submit.

Use an administrator account to see and control the clients of every user and to scan libraries. A regular user controls only their own clients.

One entry per server. Reconfigure changes the address; a revoked token starts a re-authentication.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning Polling interval 5 s How often sessions are read (2-300 s). Audio streaming codec MP3 Codec (MP3, AAC, Opus, FLAC) used when library music is streamed to another Home Assistant player through the media source.

docs.title: Data updates
docs.text: Sessions are polled at the configured interval (default 5 s): one GET /Sessions?controllableByUserId=... per poll. Every command triggers an immediate refresh, so the state follows a button press without waiting for the next poll. A failed poll makes the client entities unavailable and is logged once; a refused token (HTTP 401) starts the re-authentication flow.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src" -v ha-jellyfin-pip:/root/.cache/pip -w /src \
  python:3.14-bookworm bash -lc '
    pip install -q -r requirements-test.txt
    ruff check custom_components tests fuzz scripts
    ruff format --check custom_components tests fuzz scripts
    pytest tests -q --cov=custom_components.jellyfin_control --cov-fail-under=95
    mypy custom_components/jellyfin_control
  '

Home Assistant does not run natively on Windows (fcntl): use Docker or CI.

The tests run the real REST client against an in-memory Jellyfin (tests/conftest.py, FakeJellyfin) injected in place of the HTTP session.

fuzz/fuzz_api.py checks with Atheris that a path segment cannot escape and that the Authorization header keeps its shape whatever the device name or token.

Releases: git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z; the workflow stamps the version into the manifest of jellyfin_control.zip, which HACS installs.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
For each Jellyfin app (device) seen by the server:

Entity Purpose media_player.<device> State, artwork, metadata and every playback control the app advertises. off while the app is disconnected. remote.<device>_remote Navigation and playback commands (only for apps that accept remote control). It cannot power the app on or off: turn_on/turn_off are refused. select.<device>_audio_track Audio track of the playing item. select.<device>_subtitles Subtitles of the playing item, with off. sensor.<device>_last_played Title of the last item the app played, kept after it stops, disconnects or Home Assistant restarts. Attributes: media_content_id (to play it again), media_content_type, played_at (when the play started), and when known name, series, series_id, season, episode, album, artist, year. Only plays seen by a poll count.

On the server device:

Entity Purpose sensor.<server>_active_clients Apps playing something. sensor.<server>_connected_clients Apps connected (disabled by default). button.<server>_scan_libraries Scan every library (enabled by default for administrators only).

docs.title: Devices
docs.text: Each Jellyfin app is one device, identified by its Jellyfin device id (not its session id, which changes on every reconnection), linked to the server device. New apps appear as soon as they connect. A device that is no longer connected can be deleted from its device page.

docs.title: Media player features
docs.text:
Features follow the commands the app advertises:

Feature Needs Play, pause, stop, seek, next, previous, play media, enqueue media control support Volume set SetVolume Volume step VolumeUp and VolumeDown Mute Mute and Unmute, or ToggleMute Shuffle SetShuffleQueue Repeat SetRepeatMode Browse, search always

Extra attributes: session_id, user_name, client, client_version, host_name, last_activity, queue_size, play_method, audio_stream_index, subtitle_stream_index, media_type, and for web browsers operating_system and browser. Client IP addresses are not exposed.

docs.title: Telling clients apart
docs.text:
Jellyfin Web names every tab after its browser, so three computers all show up as "Chrome". The device name gets the machine name: the local DNS name of the client's address (reverse lookup, local addresses only, cached an hour). Without one, it gets the operating system instead. The model reads the browser and version from the User-Agent encoded in the web client's device id, e.g. Jellyfin Web · Chrome 156 · Windows. The registry follows these values on each poll; a name you set on the device is kept.

If every client shows the same machine name, Jellyfin sees the address of your reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known proxies in the Jellyfin networking settings so it records the real client address.

docs.title: Resume the next episode when you sit down
docs.text:
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.sofa_occupied
    to: "on"
actions:
  - action: jellyfin_control.browse_library
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.living_room
    data:
      parent_id: special:next_up
    response_variable: next_up
  - if: "{{ next_up['media_player.living_room'].items | count > 0 }}"
    then:
      - action: jellyfin_control.play_items
        target:
          entity_id: media_player.living_room
        data:
          item_ids: "{{ next_up['media_player.living_room'].items[0].id }}"

docs.title: Pause when the doorbell rings, and say why
docs.text:
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: binary_sensor.doorbell
    to: "on"
actions:
  - action: media_player.media_pause
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.living_room
  - action: jellyfin_control.send_message
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.living_room
    data:
      title: Doorbell
      message: Someone is at the door
      timeout: 10

docs.title: Subtitles off for movies
docs.text:
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: media_player.living_room
    attribute: media_content_id
conditions:
  - condition: state
    entity_id: media_player.living_room
    attribute: media_content_type
    state: movie
actions:
  - action: select.select_option
    target:
      entity_id: select.living_room_subtitles
    data:
      option: "off"

docs.title: Navigate with a physical remote
docs.text:
actions:
  - action: remote.send_command
    target:
      entity_id: remote.living_room_remote
    data:
      command: [down, select]
      delay_secs: 0.3

docs.title: Search and play (script with a field)
docs.text:
fields:
  title:
    selector:
      text:
sequence:
  - action: jellyfin_control.search_library
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.living_room
    data:
      query: "{{ title }}"
      limit: 1
    response_variable: found
  - action: jellyfin_control.play_items
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.living_room
    data:
      item_ids: "{{ found['media_player.living_room'].items[0].id }}"

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
HACS: add https://github.com/FiveElements/ha-jellyfin as a custom repository of type Integration, install Jellyfin Control, restart Home Assistant.

Manually: copy custom_components/jellyfin_control into your config/custom_components/ folder and restart.

Then Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → Jellyfin Control.

Requires Home Assistant 2026.11 or newer and Jellyfin 10.9 or newer.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text: Settings → Devices & services → Jellyfin Control → ⋮ → Delete. The access token is revoked on the server. Remove the files (or uninstall from HACS) and restart.

docs.title: Library browsing
docs.text:
The media panel of each Jellyfin player opens the library of the signed-in user:

  • Continue watching, Next up, Recently added, Favorites;
  • every library: movies and shows sorted by name, music split into Artists, Albums and Songs, Live TV channels, playlists, collections and plain folders;
  • a series lists its seasons, a season its episodes in airing order, an artist their albums (newest first), an album its tracks in disc order, a playlist its entries in the owner's order.

Playing a folder plays its content: a series, season, album, artist, genre, playlist or collection is expanded into a queue (at most 200 items). Search covers movies, series, episodes, albums, songs, playlists, collections and artists.

The same tree is offered as a media source (Media > Jellyfin Control), so library items can be streamed to any Home Assistant player (Cast, Sonos, browser). Videos are streamed as they are stored; music is offered in the codec chosen in the options (MP3 by default). Streams and thumbnails are relayed by Home Assistant through short-lived signed paths: the player never receives the Jellyfin token and only needs to reach Home Assistant.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Cannot connect: check the URL from the Home Assistant host (curl http://host:8096/System/Info/Public must return JSON).
  • The address now reaches another Jellyfin server: the entry refuses to start rather than send its access token to a server it was not set up with (a new DHCP lease or a proxy change). Reconfigure the entry with the right address.
  • Library actions fail with "did not match any entities": browse_library and search_library target a media player, and Home Assistant skips unavailable ones. The players become unavailable when polling sessions fails; the log says why.
  • A client is missing: only clients that the signed-in user may control are listed; sign in as an administrator to see everyone's.
  • A command does nothing: the client may not advertise it; download the diagnostics of the entry, they list each client's supported commands.
  • Enable debug logs:
logger:
  logs:
    custom_components.jellyfin_control: debug

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Sessions are polled (default every 5 s). A command triggers an immediate refresh.
  • What a client can do is what it advertises: the media player features, track selectors and actions follow its SupportedCommands. A web browser tab accepts fewer commands than the Android TV app; an action the client does not support is refused with a clear error.
  • Jellyfin clients only play items of their own library: media sources of other integrations (TTS, local files) cannot be sent to them.
  • A folder is expanded into at most 200 items (URL length), the media browser lists at most 1000 children per folder, Recently added the 100 newest items.
  • search_library returns 50 items by default, at most 500.
  • send_command and raw remote commands are sent as they are: the client ignores a command it does not know.
  • Scanning libraries needs an administrator account.
  • Jellyfin has no discovery protocol Home Assistant can use: the address is entered by hand.
